history.period: Present-day structure modern; traditional Durga Puja here said to be over a century old per local accounts (verify)
history.summary: Durga Badi, beside the Firayalal building at Albert Ekka Chowk in the heart of Ranchi, is one of the city's oldest and most traditional Durga Puja sites — reviewers describe a ritual, traditional Bengali-style Durga Puja conducted here for more than 100 years, with the idol, prasad and traditions unchanged across generations (local claim, verify). It functions as a temple complex with sub-shrines of Kali, Shiva, Ganesh and Radha-Krishna, and draws devotees of all communities. The idol is taken out on devotees' shoulders for immersion at Bada Talaab. No published history of the temple's founding or construction date could be found; only the living Durga Puja tradition is documented.

name: Durga Badi
town_description: Ranchi is the capital and largest city of Jharkhand, set on the Chota Nagpur Plateau. Known as the 'City of Waterfalls', it grew from a summer retreat of the Bengal administration into a major industrial and administrative centre.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi — about 7 km south of the city centre
travel.railway: Ranchi Junction — about 2.5 km southeast of the temple
travel.road: Central Ranchi location beside Firayalal/Albert Ekka Chowk; easily reached by city bus, auto-rickshaw and taxi

visitor_information.best_time: October-November during Durga Puja; October-February for pleasant weather
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not published; typically open daily for morning and evening worship (verify)
